answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every new agent to post a refundable stake that is locked for a full epoch and can only be reclaimed after a rotating set of established peers attests its work. A fable of free identities dies here: creating a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand stakes, and any proven forgery burns the stake and taints the whole cluster. Like a raven that remembers faces, the network keeps an umber-stained ledger of past fraud, so repeat offenders face higher bonds and longer lockups, making mass fakery cost more than any reward it could harvest.
